Alex — quick technical checklist and recommendations (for SREs). I kept it pragmatic with examples.

1) Cluster sizing and node classes- Minimum node types:
  * control-plane: 3 x m4.large-equivalent (HA control plane)
  * inference-pool (cpu/gpu mix): 8 x p4-like GPU nodes (each 1x GPU, 96GB RAM) for steady 200 qps; plan for autoscale to 24 nodes for burst to 600 qps.
  * utils/ops: 2 x 16GB worker nodes for logging/sidecars

2) Storage guidance- KV cache: use ephemeral local NVMe on inference nodes, provision ~500GB per node to keep warm caches (depends on model KV size).
  - Persistent volumes: Rook/Ceph block storage recommended for model artifacts and long-term checkpointing. PV class: ceph-block-retain, typical sizes 2TB+ per model repository.
  - Ephemeral scratch: hostPath-backed emptyDir with local SSD for inference temp files.
  - Backup/archive: SAN for cold models, S3-compatible object store for snapshots.

3) PV and IO characteristics- Use RBD (Rook) with provisioned IOPS; ensure Ceph pool has at least 3x replication or erasure coding per policy. Tune rbd_defaults for read-heavy workloads.

4) Networking- Required egress rules:
  * allow outbound TCP to update.redwood.internal:443, metrics.redwood.internal:443 (for model rollouts, healthheartbeats)
  * allow NTP and DNS (UDP 123, TCP/UDP 53)
  * intra-cluster: Calico or Cilium allowed; we recommend Cilium for BPF performance.
  * MTU: if you use overlay, pick jumbo MTU 9000 and test for fragmentation.

5) Security- KMS integration: supports customer-managed keys via Vault HSM or cloud KMS gateway.
  - Audit logs: forward token-level audit logs to your SIEM; redact PII per policy.
  - RBAC: create a dedicated ServiceAccount for Redwood runtime with least privilege.

6) Deployment & rollbacks- Canary approach: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automatic fallback to hosted cluster if local capacity breach.

Attachments: redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf (contains YAML snippets: StorageClass, StatefulSet example for model-service, Ceph RBD StorageClass template).

If helpful, we can include sample resource requests/limits for the inference pods and a small test harness to simulate 200 qps at 1.2k seq to validate IO.

—Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
